fiveYear.note: Full years. First half 2026: revenue RM2.04bn (-29%) as big data-centre jobs neared completion, but profit RM222m (+39%) on better margins and write-backs.

rows.name: Construction
rows.tip: Data centres, buildings, infrastructure and fit-out work in Malaysia, Singapore and India.

rows.tip: Factory-made concrete parts, mainly for Singapore public housing.

segments.note: Half-year to 30 June 2026, revenue from outside customers (Q2 p.10).

assets.label: Money owed by customers and others

liabilities.label: Owed to subcontractors, suppliers and others

balance.note: Still cash-rich: RM1.6bn of cash against RM0.4bn of borrowings at June 2026. Equity fell to RM0.7bn because the special dividend paid out more than the half-year's profit (Q2 p.5).

cash.wfNote: In the first half of 2026 SunCon paid RM725m of dividends, including the 23 sen special, far more than the RM202m of cash its operations produced; cash fell to RM1.6bn.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM10.3 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM24 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 incl. 23 sen special)
metrics.plain: FY2025 dividends including a one-off 23 sen special. Without it, the regular 27.5 sen gives about 3.5%.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: FY2025 dividends of 50.5 sen against last-12-month profit: above 100% because of the special dividend.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 16.7 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM61 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 1H2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM10.88.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Net cash
metrics.plain: Cash and investments minus borrowings: RM1,208 million. Positive means no net debt.

metrics.label: Free cash flow 1H2026
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM199 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

drivers.evidence: Order book at an all-time high of RM10.5bn; RM6.85bn won in 2026, target raised to RM7-9bn (Q2 p.19)
drivers.why: Gives strong earnings visibility for the next two years.

drivers.evidence: Data centres are 70% of the order book; three new data-centre jobs in 1H2026 (Q2 p.19, p.25)
drivers.why: AI and cloud demand keep the pipeline full.

drivers.evidence: 1H2026 revenue fell 29% as earlier data-centre jobs neared completion (Q2 p.3, p.25)
drivers.why: New jobs take time to ramp up; revenue should recover as they progress.

drivers.evidence: Profit to shareholders +39% despite lower revenue (Q2 p.3)
RM19m net write-back of impairments helped 1H2026 profit (Q2 p.3)
23% of the order book from parent projects like the RTS TOD and Sunway Ipoh Mall (Q2 p.25)
drivers.why: A stable base of work; tied to Sunway's own plans.

drivers.evidence: Precast revenue doubled to RM148m in 1H2026 (Q2 p.10)
GDP grew 6.0% and construction 6.5% in Q2 2026 (Q2 p.19)
Higher electricity tariffs, wages and material prices (AR p.13)
drivers.why: Fixed-price contracts lose margin when costs rise.

drivers.evidence: Data-centre jobs for a few multinational clients dominate the order book (Q2 p.25)
drivers.why: Delays or cancellations by one client would matter.

drivers.evidence: RM1.6bn cash vs RM0.4bn borrowings at June 2026 (Q2 p.5)
RM725m of dividends paid in 1H2026, including the 23 sen special (Q2 p.7)
drivers.why: Generous, but the special part may not repeat.

drivers.evidence: About 24 times last-12-month profit at RM7.81 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: The price assumes the data-centre wave continues.

suppliers: Mechanical, electrical, piling and fit-out trades; most of the RM1.8bn operating costs in 1H2026
Steel, concrete and cables, including inputs for its precast factories
Some services and amounts owed within the Sunway group
Short-term trade financing and loans: RM430m of borrowings at June 2026
customers: Data centres in Johor and Serendah: 70% of the RM10.5bn order book
Hospitals, malls and transit-oriented developments: 23% of the order book
Precast concrete parts for public housing projects: 7% of the order book
RTS Link to Singapore; a highway project in India

outlook.text: All-time-high RM10.5bn order book provides strong earnings visibility; 2026 order target raised to RM7-9bn (Q2 p.19).
AI and cloud adoption expected to sustain a healthy pipeline of data-centre investment in Malaysia (Q2 p.19).
Will stay selective, prioritising projects with healthy margins and achievable timelines (Q2 p.19).
Cost pressures from electricity tariffs, wages and materials (AR p.13).

outlookOverall.text: Management points to a record order book and a strong data-centre pipeline (Q2 p.19).
